assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new organising principle for electronic phases: band topology, protected edge and surface states and the Z2 classification, joining a clear theoretical idea with a decisive experiment. Its influence on electronic-structure theory, materials search and spintronics is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state in graphene with the Z2 invariant, and Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. This is a compact and defensible three-person configuration. Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang) and for 3D topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele; Hasan) lies outside or partly outside the credited names and complicates allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed by many independent groups and materials families (HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3-type compounds, ARPES and transport) over roughly 15 to 20 years, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should include 3D topological insulators and the ARPES work or only the quantum spin Hall effect, and who then belongs.
The omitted theorists of the HgTe prediction (one now deceased) make the credit story incomplete; my recollection of the details is not independently verified.
Practical applications remain mostly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity there created the moire materials field, a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Originality and scientific impact are very high and unusually clean as a theory-plus-experiment pair.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states. This forms a natural three-person prize. Contributions of other experimental groups, and of Cao as lead author, are not representable here.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: widely reproduced across groups and extended to many moire systems, but the microscopic nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, and the field is only about eight years old.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the origin of the correlated phases remain unsettled, which may argue for waiting.
Sensitivity of experimental results to sample twist-angle disorder is a known concern.
Whether credit should be extended to the other experimental groups and to the graphene-systems theorists is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and local correlations exactly in infinite dimensions and combining with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) to treat real materials. Its impact on correlated-electron theory and computational materials science is deep and long-lasting. I declare that this lies close to my own working area, and I have weighed that.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping to the Anderson impurity model and the DFT+DMFT extension; Vollhardt contributed to the early development of the infinite-dimensional limit. Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, and Müller-Hartmann, Jarrell and Rozenberg also made important contributions. The three-name configuration is plausible but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than 30 years of use, benchmarked against experiments and numerics, with many extensions (cluster DMFT, DFT+DMFT for materials). Because it is a method, Nobel-criteria fit (discovery or invention with demonstrable benefit) is open to debate.
uncertainties: Theory-heavy: no single decisive experiment, so the committee may regard it as a tool rather than a discovery.
Approximate nature (local self-energy) and sensitivity to double-counting choices in DFT+DMFT limit quantitative predictivity.
Allocation among Metzner, Vollhardt, Georges, Kotliar and others is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later large TMR in crystalline MgO barriers, underlies modern read heads and MRAM. It is a natural successor to the giant magnetoresistance prize, with a clear physical mechanism (spin-dependent tunnelling and symmetry filtering, supported by first-principles calculations) and major technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Yuasa (and Parkin, not listed) demonstrated giant TMR in MgO-based junctions in 2004. The three credited names form a clear configuration, though Julliere's early work and the MgO theory contributors (Butler, Mathon) fall outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: roughly 30 years of reproduction and commercialisation, with a stable interpretation. Timing is good, though the 2007 GMR prize may make the committee view it as partly recognised already.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize and whether this adds enough as a new discovery.
Parkin's MgO work is not among the credited names, so attribution of the decisive MgO result is incomplete.
The theory of coherent tunnelling is credited to others not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures that connect magnetism, topology and spintronics. Their observation in MnSi and in thin films, and their current-driven motion, opened a significant area of research in noncollinear magnetism that I know well from atomistic spin-dynamics work.
assessment.attribution: The decisive early observation in bulk MnSi came from the Pfleiderer group (Mühlbauer, Böni and others), real-space imaging of skyrmions in thin films from Tokura's group, and a skyrmion lattice at an atomic-scale interface from Wiesendanger's group. The theory (Bogdanov, Rößler) is not represented in the credit, which undermines a fair prize. Roughly one-third of the central contributors are absent or unclear.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: widely confirmed, but device-level promise remains largely unrealised and the field is still evolving. Some years more of evidence on applications may be useful.
uncertainties: Missing theoretical founders (Bogdanov and collaborators) and experimentalists (Mühlbauer, Böni) in the credited names.
Application relevance remains unproven.
Dispute over which of the first observations should be recognised as decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nd-Fe-B magnets remain the strongest commercial permanent magnets and underpin wind turbines, electric vehicles and drives and a wide range of electronics. This is a major invention with massive societal impact, and it rests on the intrinsic magnetism of the Nd2Fe14B phase, which electronic-structure theory later explained.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo, sintered magnets) and Croat (General Motors, melt-spun magnets) independently announced the material in 1983-84, so a two-person configuration is natural. Other contributors to the intrinsic properties (e.g. Herbst) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with four decades of use. The question is whether it is physics rather than materials science or engineering, but Nobel's will emphasises invention and benefit to humankind, so recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently a physics discovery rather than a materials-engineering one.
Priority and credit between the two groups and corporate contributions.
Reliance on rare earths affects relevance but not scientific merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetoelectric multiferroics combine magnetic and ferroelectric order and allow electrical control of magnetism. The conceptual question of why ferroelectricity and magnetism tend to be mutually exclusive, answered by first-principles theory, plus the BiFeO3 and TbMnO3 experiments, constitutes a coherent and valuable body of work in correlated oxides.
assessment.attribution: Spaldin gave the foundational theoretical analysis and DFT predictions (e.g. BiFeO3, with Ramesh's group providing thin-film realisation), and Tokura's group discovered magnetically induced ferroelectricity in TbMnO3. Other pioneers (Schmid, Kimura, Cheong, Hill/Spaldin on the mutual-exclusion question) are not credited; the three-name set is reasonable but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Intermediate: well-confirmed physics but the technological promise (magnetoelectric devices) has not been realised, and room-temperature strong coupling is limited, which makes the case for impact less compelling at present.
uncertainties: Device impact remains largely prospective.
Credit between Cheong, Kimura, Tokura and others for the TbMnO3 discovery is unresolved.
Tokura already appears on other candidates, so overlap is a consideration for composing a balanced prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third fundamental class of collinear magnetism, with zero net magnetisation and spin-split bands arising from crystal symmetry. It is conceptually elegant and is likely to be consequential for spintronics, and as a magnetism theorist I find the symmetry classification persuasive.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth articulated the symmetry classification and unified the earlier piecemeal results in 2019-2022, with earlier related work by others (e.g. Hayami, Yuan and Zunger, Ahn). A three-name configuration is conceivable, but the early-priority question is real.
assessment.maturity: Premature relative to other candidates: the concept is only about four years old, with ARPES and magnetic-circular-dichroism confirmations in MnTe and CrSb appearing since 2024. It remains early for a prize, and I rank it eighth for this reason.
uncertainties: Short track record and still-evolving experimental confirmation.
Priority conflicts with earlier theoretical work by others.
Technological relevance not yet demonstrated.
